## Video-Catcher 0.7.0: sites behind a bot check

Many sites sit behind a wall (mostly Cloudflare) that lets browsers in and turns everything else away. Videos from such sites failed with "The site refused the download" or "The site no longer accepts the link", although the stream was found. This release is about them. **The window and the extension both changed: update both.**

- **New:** when a site turns the download away (HTTP 403, or it names its bot check), Video-Catcher tries once more, answering the way your browser does. The list says "site wants a browser, trying as one". Only then comes the page the video was found on, as before.
- **New:** the extension passes along the proof that the bot check let your browser in (cookies like `cf_clearance`), with every video and page, also without **Send the site's login (cookies) along**. These cookies are no login. All other cookies still only leave the browser with that option.
- **New:** **Copy a report** in the extension's window, for a video the extension does not find. It lists what the extension saw on the page; links are shortened, so no key and no login is in it. Add it to an issue.
- **New:** the extension also sees a stream that a player loads through a frame of its own to stay out of sight.
- **Changed:** clearer messages. A bot check is named as one ("The site checks for a real browser and did not let Video-Catcher in"). "yt-dlp does not know this site" now says what to do: send a stream from the extension's list instead of the page or the player.
- **Changed:** "What yt-dlp said" keeps the lines of every try, not only of the last one.
- **Changed:** in the extension's list, a **PLAYER** entry and the "stream out of sight" note now say that a page or a player only works for sites yt-dlp knows.

What it still cannot do: get around DRM, pass a bot check your own browser does not pass, or download what your login cannot play in the browser. On Windows on ARM, yt-dlp may come without the part for answering like a browser; the message then says so.

Files: `VideoCatcher.exe` (or `VideoCatcher-arm64.exe`) and the extension (`VideoCatcher-extension-chromium.zip`, `VideoCatcher-extension-firefox.zip` or `.xpi`). After updating the extension, reload the pages that were already open.

The files are not digitally signed yet; Windows SmartScreen may warn. Every file is built by GitHub Actions from this repository, and `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists their checksums.
